title: How Paul Buchheit hires: ask questions you can't answer and hire people smarter than you
summary: A Standard Capital chat on startup hiring. Paul Buchheit (Google employee 23, Gmail creator, FriendFeed founder) explains how he interviewed at early Google, using a hard open problem that surfaced Noam Shazeer, and why you should hire people who make you better.

principles.text: Interview with the hardest problem you haven't fully solved yourself, not a stock question.
principles.quote: one of the things I always like to do is just work on one of the hardest problems. What are the things I don't know.

principles.text: Use an unsolved problem from your own work as the interview question; it can reveal someone far ahead of you.
principles.quote: there was one person I interviewed who immediately was like amazing right there in the interview he was already ahead of where I was thinking. And so, I said like, we have to hire this guy

principles.text: Don't be afraid to pose the hardest questions, and look for people smarter than you.
principles.quote: don't be afraid to pose the hardest questions and um you know, generally you want to look for people who are smarter than you are.

principles.text: A's hire A's, B's hire C's: insecure people avoid strong hires, ambitious people want to be surrounded by people who inspire them.
principles.quote: if you're someone who's who's actually really smart and and you're ambitious, you want to surround yourself with other people who will who will inspire you and will you can actually learn from.

principles.text: Judge each interview by whether you learned something; if not, it was a bad interview.
principles.quote: at the end of the interview, I ask myself, what did I learn? If the answer is nothing, then it's a bad interview.
